### Problem

The release candidate v7.19.0 fails the release scenario `settled-rerun` in what the engine did: its `until` or `expect` did not hold, or could no longer hold, so the lane releases nothing and `v7` stays where it is.
Reproduced by: https://github.com/DiluxOne/.github/actions/runs/44642022228 scenario `settled-rerun`.

Cause, verified twice (lane runs 44809827873 and 44817376834): the review's concurrency group cancels by the order jobs reach it, not by the commit they review. The scenario opens the pull request and pushes the token 5 seconds later, so two runs of "Pull request (test repository)" start: `opened` at the first commit and `synchronize` at the token's. In DiluxOne/diluxone-test#3459 the token's review job (0fb9c65, run 44817583104) started at 21:08:20 and was cancelled at 21:08:22 ("A task was canceled"), because the first commit's review job (c500e8b, run 44817577119) reached the same group, `claude-review-<repo>-<pr>-code` with `cancel-in-progress: true` (claude-review.yml, about line 138), later, at 21:08:24. That older job then reviewed c500e8b, which has no token, so nothing blocked, and the head's review check stayed cancelled, failing `pipeline` ("fix the failed check"). The same happened in #3392 (5bab4ba cancelled at 20:18:09, 6d139e4 reviewed). It is not the scenario's alone: any pull request pushed to right after it opens can end with its head never reviewed. The fix: a review job for a commit that is no longer the pull request's head must not run or cancel anything (for example a job before it that reads the current head and skips the review when it differs, so the stale job never joins the group), and the head's review always runs. Plus a test that would have caught it.

### Scope

- The cause of the failure above, in the engine, fixed with a test that would have caught it.

### Out of scope

- Changing the gates or what they check.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given v7.19.0's candidate with the fix, when the release lane plays `settled-rerun` in the test repository, then it passes and the lane releases it.

### Criticality

Critical
